title: Keppard record date: Stockyard Blues
summary: Taylor recalls the Keppard date: Stockyard Blues was his, with Camel on piano, Vinson on trombone, a twelve-piece band and Johnny Dodds on clarinet.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yeah, well, Stockyard Blues, that's mine. I just simply had my, played over on the Zillophone and Freddie, got the boys together. And, you know, it didn't take very long before they fall in. Yes.
Can you remember who else was on the date?
Well, uh, let me see, I know Camel was on piano, and, uh, I know the, the trombone player, but I just can't call his name just now. I'm trying to think too, but that's-
Vinson. Yes, Vinson, he was on the.
It was about a twelve piece band.
Was it that big? Yeah. How do you know it was that big?
Oh, yeah. We had, uh, see there's about that, quite a few on the basses.
I think we played that record for you up at John Steiner's, oh, several years ago when I was living up there. And if I remember rightly, you identified Johnny Dodds as the clarinetist.
Yeah. And then we had, uh, now we're playing the wood blocks.
Yeah. Uh, did you play washboard on any of that date, or either one of those? No, no, no.
